Latest UPPSC, 2019–23

Facts asked in the newest UPPSC papers, newest year first.

UPPSC 2023

  • Voluntary social service = not an economic activity. →
  • UN Secretary General presents annual SDG Progress Report (global indicator framework, national data). →
  • Using natural resources with minimum degradation = sustainable development. →
  • Balancing resource use with conservation for future = sustainable development. →
  • Reforms needed to feed population; many farmers still rely on monsoon and soil fertility (true, not reason). →
  • Nandini Krishak Samriddhi Yojana (UP, Nand Baba Mission): only Sahiwal, Gir, Tharparkar, Gangatiri cows. →
  • MPEDA: set up by Act of Parliament, 1972; HQ Kochi (not Kolkata). →
  • PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan: launched 13 Oct 2021; multi-modal connectivity. →
  • UP sugar problems: low cane yield, short crushing season, poor mill location. →
  • ES 2022-23: fashion, grocery, general merchandise ~2/3 of e-commerce market by 2027 (not 2030). →
  • Budget 2023-24: States allowed fiscal deficit 3.5% of GSDP (0.5% tied to power reforms). →
  • ITC (Input Tax Credit): credit of tax paid on inputs by registered person; avoids cascading. →
  • UP Budget 2023-24: size Rs 6,90,242 crore (not 7.6 lakh crore); fiscal deficit Rs 84,883.16 crore. →
  • Order: 14-bank nationalization → RRBs → 6-bank nationalization → NABARD. →
  • PIN = Personal Identification Number. →
  • Accounting = language of business; gives all information a businessman needs. →
  • Condition = essential term, breach lets party reject contract; warranty = side term, breach gives only damages. →
  • Budget 2023-24: PMKVY 4.0; 30 Skill India International Centres. →
  • JSY aim: cut maternal and neonatal deaths via institutional delivery. →
  • SP Mukherji Rurban Mission: 2016, not 2015. →
  • Budget 2023-24: biggest cut Atma Nirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana; biggest rise Reform Linked Distribution Scheme. →
  • Mid-day Meal renamed PM POSHAN, 2021. →

    Chapter 1

    Nature of Indian Economy

    India is a mixed, developing economy; its main features and reforms.

    UPPSC asks most here

    1. Mixed economy: public sector and private sector co-exist; govt encourages both.PCS Pre ’90; PCS Mains ’13; UDA/LDA ’99, ’064 papers
    2. Indian economy = prominent example of mixed economy (not socialist, capitalist or Gandhian).PCS Pre ’07; PCS Pre (Re-exam) ’15; PCS Mains ’13; RO/ARO Mains ’164 papers
    3. India = developing economy (now "middle income developing market economy").PCS Pre ’95; PCS Mains ’112 papers
    4. Indian model of development protects interest of both State (public sector) and person (private sector).UDA/LDA ’131 paper
    5. Underdeveloped economy: low per capita income, low capital formation, high population growth, poverty, illiteracy.PCS Mains ’171 paper

    Mixed Economy

    • Mixed economy: public sector and private sector co-exist; govt encourages both.UPPSC ×4
    • Blends capitalism + socialism; private property allowed, govt regulates for social aims.
    • Indian economy = prominent example of mixed economy (not socialist, capitalist or Gandhian).UPPSC ×4
    • Gandhian economy: decentralisation, equal sharing of resources, self-employment, self-reliance.
    • Indian model of development protects interest of both State (public sector) and person (private sector).UPPSC

    Developing Economy Features

    • India = labour-surplus economy: huge population, many workers at subsistence wage.
    • India projected skilled-labour surplus ~245.3 million by 2030.
    • Underdeveloped economy: low per capita income, low capital formation, high population growth, poverty, illiteracy.UPPSC
    • Low dependency ratio and workforce mostly in tertiary sector = features of developed economy.
    • Also underdeveloped signs: unequal income, high dependency ratio, slow national income growth.
    • India = developing economy (now "middle income developing market economy").UPPSC ×2
    • Developing features: mainly agriculture, disguised unemployment (extra workers adding no output), poor human capital.UPPSC
    • Also: low technology, weak infrastructure, poverty, inequality, market imperfections.
    • Indian economy: agriculture dominates, low per capita income, massive unemployment; industry does not dominate.UPPSC
    • Lack of natural resources NOT a feature (low labour productivity, low capital formation are).UPPSC

    Economic Activity

    • Economic activity: resources (capital, labour) → production → goods/services; e.g. farming, transport, services.
    • Voluntary social service = not an economic activity.UPPSC
    • Economic factors of development: natural/energy resources, labour, capital formation, technology, capital-output ratio, organisation.
    • Non-economic factors: social, religious, political, international, scientific; e.g. social behaviour.

    Second Generation Reforms

    • Second Generation Reforms: oil sector, public sector, govt and public institutions; not legal/judicial system.UPPSC

    Chapter 2

    National Income and GDP

    National income concepts, formulas, estimating agencies, base years, growth data, per capita income and savings.

    UPPSC asks most here

    1. GDP growth 1998-99: 6.5% (base 1993-94); revised 6.7%.PCS Pre ’97, ’99, ’00, ’05; PCS Mains ’03, ’05; Lower Sub (Spl) ’02, ’038 papers
    2. GDP growth 2005-06 (1999-2000 prices) 8.4% → 8–9% band; later revised 9.5%.PCS Pre ’01, ’03, ’06; PCS Mains ’14; UDA/LDA ’02; RI ’146 papers
    3. Hindu rate of growth: term by Raj Krishna (1981); slow ~3.5% national income/GDP growth, 1950s–80s.PCS Pre ’96, ’06; PCS Mains ’043 papers
    4. 1990–2000 · 1999-2000 (8.8%)PCS Pre ’02; Lower Sub (Spl) ’02, ’033 papers
    5. Bihar (lowest) · 47,498PCS Pre ’93, ’08; Lower Sub ’043 papers

    National Income Formulas

    • National Income (NI) = NNP at factor cost (FC).
    • NI = GNP(MP) − depreciation − indirect taxes + subsidies.
    • NNP(MP) = GNP(MP) − depreciation.
    • NI = NNP(MP) − (indirect taxes − subsidies); indirect taxes − subsidy = Net Indirect Taxes (NIT).
    • GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad (NFI); so NNP = GDP + NFI − depreciation.
    • NDP = GDP − depreciation (not plus).
    • MP = market prices; FC = factor cost; D = depreciation.
    • National income = money value of final goods and services by normal residents in a year.
    • GNP: output of a nation's normal residents, inside or outside country.
    • Open economy: Y = C + I + G + (X − M); X − M = net exports.
    • 3 methods of GDP: product, income, expenditure (no "diminishing cost method").
    • Nominal GDP: GDP at current market prices, no inflation adjustment; used for GDP deflator.
    • NDP better than GDP for comparing world economies (shows depreciation cost).
    • Per Capita Income = National Income (NNP) ÷ total population.
    • Personal Disposable Income (PDI) = personal income − personal tax payments.
    • Prices and money income both double → real income unchanged.UPPSC
    • Problems in counting NI in India: unorganised sector (main), poor data, double counting, non-monetised sector, black money.

    Growth vs Development

    • Economic growth measured by GDP, GNP, per capita GNP; World Bank aid not counted.
    • Amartya Sen (Nobel 1998, welfare economics): planning should focus on people, not commodities.UPPSC
    • Sen's priorities: people-oriented, security for poorest, safeguards on world integration.UPPSC
    • Hindu rate of growth: term by Raj Krishna (1981); slow ~3.5% national income/GDP growth, 1950s–80s.UPPSC ×3
    • Economic growth usually comes with inflation.
    • Labour share in GNP low because wages lag behind prices.UPPSC
    • Economic growth vs development: growth = output rise; development = growth + better living standard.
    • Real GNP rise ≠ development if poverty and unemployment increase.
    • Business cycle: boom (high activity) → recession (gradual fall) → depression (drastic fall) → recovery (steady rise).
    • Meltdown = steep fall in stock prices; recession = big contraction; slowdown = fall in activity.
    • Public sector share in GDP declined in decade to 2010; private share rose.
    • Factors of growth: natural resources, physical capital, population/labour, human capital, technology, law.
    • Technocrats and bureaucrats = not a major factor of growth.UPPSC
    • Best measure of growth/development: sustained rise in real per capita income (per capita product).UPPSC ×2
    • Per capita income represents standard of living.UPPSC
    • Per capita income growth at current prices > constant prices; constant prices remove price rise.
    • Real sector: production of goods/services (farming, textile mills); bank lending, bond issue = financial sector.

    New Economic Policy 1991

    • NEP 1991 strategy = LPG: Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation.UPPSC
    • Criticism of NEP mostly due to ideological differences.
    • Liberalisation began with changes in industrial licensing; New Industrial Policy 24 July 1991 (Narasimha Rao govt).
    • 1991 policy: all industries freed from licence except 18.
    • Dr. Manmohan Singh (then Finance Minister) = pioneer of liberalisation.
    • Stabilisation: demand side, short-term (inflation, fiscal, BoP); structural adjustment: supply side, long-term, gradual.
    • Occupational structure unchanged as investment went to capital-intensive industries.

    Estimating Agencies & Base Year

    • Dadabhai Naoroji: first estimate of national income, 1867-68; per capita income Rs. 20.UPPSC ×2
    • First scientific estimate: V.K.R.V. Rao, 1931-32.
    • National Income Committee 1949: chairman P.C. Mahalanobis; members D.R. Gadgil, V.K.R.V. Rao.UPPSC
    • CSO set up 1951; estimated national income earlier.
    • NSO formed 2019 by merging CSO and NSSO; now estimates and releases national income.
    • Capital formation data: RBI and CSO (now NSO); K.N. Raj Committee (1981) fixed roles.UPPSC
    • Base year: year whose prices are used to calculate real GDP (constant prices).
    • Base year changed 2004-05 → 2011-12 (CSO, 2015); present base year 2011-12.UPPSC ×2
    • New series: GVA at basic prices replaced GDP at factor cost; follows UN SNA 2008 (not 1994).
    • CSO series of Feb 1999 used base 1993-94.UPPSC
    • Earlier base years: 1999-2000 (around 2009), 2004-05 (around 2010).
    • Development needs multi-dimensional approach; govt focuses on both micro and macro issues.UPPSC
    • Macro issues: CAD, fiscal deficit, inflation, employment, BoP; micro: firm, price, consumption.

    Capital Formation & Savings

    • Capital formation: net capital build-up; depends on savings, investment, effective financial institutions.UPPSC
    • Capital-output ratio (COR): capital needed per unit of output; high COR → low growth.
    • G = S ÷ C (growth = savings ÷ COR); high COR from poor technology or management.
    • Slow per capita income growth: high COR + fast population growth.
    • Capital formation = most important factor for growth.
    • Highest gross domestic savings 2001–10: 2007-08 (37.8% of GDP).UPPSC
    • Savings 2006-07: 34.9% of GDP (above 32%).UPPSC
    • Savings rate: 2012-13 33.9%; 2020-21 28.83%; 2021-22 30.15%.
    • Household sector = largest contributor to savings.UPPSC ×2
    • Corporate sector savings share rose in early 2000s (3.4% → 10.2%).UPPSC
    • Household savings: physical assets largest share (more than deposits, currency, shares).UPPSC
    • Savings order: household > private corporate > public enterprises > government.UPPSC

    Chapter 3

    Sustainable Economic Development

    SDGs and India's ranks, meaning of sustainable development, human capital and inclusive growth.

    UPPSC asks most here

    1. NITI Aayog = nodal institution for SDGs (Agenda 2030) in India.PCS Pre ’191 paper

    Limits to Growth

    • Limits to Growth concept: Club of Rome (born April 1968, Rome); report 1972.UPPSC
    • Meadows (1972): limits reached in 100 years if trends continue; revised to 30 years in 2004.
    • Environmental Kuznets Curve: per capita GDP vs environmental damage; inverted U shape.UPPSC

    Sustainable Development Meaning

    • Term first used 1980 by IUCN (World Conservation Strategy).
    • Brundtland Report "Our Common Future" (1987, WCED): meets present needs without harming future generations' needs.UPPSC
    • Definition: saving energy and resources for future without sacrificing present comfort.UPPSC
    • Using natural resources with minimum degradation = sustainable development.UPPSC
    • Balancing resource use with conservation for future = sustainable development.UPPSC
    • Linked with carrying capacity: max population an area can sustain.
    • Base of sustainable development = environmental approach.
    • It is inter-generational sensitivity on use of natural resources.UPPSC
    • Neemrana (Alwar, Rajasthan) = model of sustainable economic development.UPPSC
    • Sustainable tourism: manage tourism and environment, keep cultural integrity and ecological processes.UPPSC
    • India-Norway Task Force on Blue Economy: launched January 2019.
    • First chapter on sustainable development and climate change: Economic Survey 2011-12.UPPSC

    Human and Social Capital

    • Social capital: mutual trust and harmony in society.
    • Human capital formation: raising people's knowledge, skills, capacities; = intangible wealth.
    • Accumulating capital and tangible wealth = physical capital (gross capital formation).
    • Skill development programme enhances human capital.UPPSC
    • India adds ~12 million to workforce yearly; 711 million aged 15-59.
    • PMKVY: flagship skill scheme of Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.
    • Education, medical care, training build human capital; irrigation has no direct impact.UPPSC
    • Human capital investment → skill development → proper resource use → higher productivity.UPPSC
    • Human Capital Index (World Bank, 2018): 2020 top Singapore (0.88); India 116th (115th of 157 in 2018).

    Inclusive Growth

    • Inclusive growth: growth shared fairly by all; pro-poor; needs infrastructure, agriculture revival, education, health.UPPSC
    • High national income growth alone does not ensure inclusive growth.UPPSC
    • Inclusive growth aided by SHGs, MSMEs, Right to Education Act.
    • Inclusive governance: District Planning Committees, public health spending, Mid-day Meal; not NBFC banking.

    Chapter 4

    Agriculture and Allied Sectors

    Indian agriculture: land reforms, share in GDP, crops, schemes, revolutions, insurance, MSP and farm credit.

    UPPSC asks most here

    1. Share of agriculture in GDP declining since Planning began: above 50% (1950-51) → 14.1% (2011-12).PCS Pre ’99; PCS Mains ’17; Lower Sub ’043 papers
    2. CAG report 2000: food subsidy Rs. 2,800 cr (1992-93) → Rs. 8,700 cr (1998-99), 3.1 times.PCS Pre ’01, ’03; UDA/LDA ’023 papers
    3. Kisan Credit Card: 1998-99; NABARD model on R.V. Gupta Committee advice.PCS Mains (Spl) ’08; RO/ARO Mains ’14; GIC ’103 papers
    4. Foodgrains: 50.8 mn t (1950-51) → 211.9 mn t (2001-02); near self-sufficiency, little bulk import.PCS Pre ’03; UDA/LDA ’022 papers
    5. Low productivity causes: population pressure, small holdings, disguised unemployment, monsoon dependence; not co-operative farming.PCS Pre ’07; UDA/LDA ’022 papers

    Basics and Farm Policy

    • Kisan Divas: 23 December, birth anniversary of PM Chaudhary Charan Singh.UPPSC
    • Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce Act 2020: trade outside APMC mandis; no State fee outside APMC; repealed 1 Dec 2021.
    • Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act 2020 and contract farming Act 2020 also repealed 1 Dec 2021.
    • Union Budget 2020-21: 16 action points on agriculture, irrigation, rural development; aim doubling farmers' income by 2022.UPPSC
    • Budget 2020-21 gave Rs. 2.83 lakh crore to agriculture, irrigation, rural development.
    • Genetic industry: breeding plants/animals for sale; e.g. agriculture, nurseries, poultry, pisciculture.UPPSC
    • Food management aims: procurement, distribution, buffer stock; not export.
    • PDS, MSP, buffer stock all improve agricultural marketing.
    • Rice price affected by MSP, govt trading, stockpiling, consumer subsidies; OMSS sale checks inflation.
    • Public investment in agriculture: cold storage, PACS computerisation, social capital; not MSP, free power, loan waiver.
    • PM-KISAN: Central Sector scheme, 100% Centre; from 1.12.2018; announced Interim Budget 1 Feb 2019.
    • PM-KISAN launched 24 Feb 2019 at Gorakhpur (UP); Rs. 6,000/year in 3 instalments to landholding families.
    • eNAM: pan-India electronic trading portal linking APMC mandis; quality-based prices.

    Land Reforms and Holdings

    • Charan Singh opposed co-operative farming (Nehru's Soviet-style model).UPPSC
    • Small Farmer Large Field: small farmers group and synchronise farm operations; IRRI pilot in Odisha.
    • Bullock capitalist (Rudolphs, 1987): self-employed farmer with some resources, not rich.UPPSC
    • Land reforms: Zamindari abolition, ceiling on holdings, tenancy reforms; not multiple cropping.UPPSC
    • Abolition of intermediaries, tenancy reforms, land ceiling made agrarian structure growth-friendly.UPPSC
    • Tenancy reforms: rent regulation, security of tenure, ownership to tenants.UPPSC

    • Most holders: UP (23.82 mn) > Bihar > Maharashtra; most area: Rajasthan (20.87 mn ha) > Maharashtra > UP.

    Crops and Production

    • Soyabean largest area: Madhya Pradesh (5.21 mn ha, Kharif 2023) > Maharashtra > Rajasthan.UPPSC

    • Cotton yield highest in India: Rajasthan (590 kg/ha, 2023-24).
    • Black soil (Regur, black cotton soil): best for cotton; Deccan; holds moisture long.UPPSC
    • Wheat output: 109.52 mn t (2020-21, 4th A.E.); 112.02 mn t (2023-24, 2nd A.E.).
    • Wheat order then: Haryana > MP > Rajasthan > Bihar; 2022-23: UP (34.91 mn t) > MP > Punjab.UPPSC
    • Rice 2022-23: Telangana > West Bengal > UP > Punjab.

    • Net irrigated area 71.6 mn ha (2018-19).
    • Cropping intensity = gross cropped ÷ net sown; ~135% (2009-10: 135.79%); 141.6% (2018-19).UPPSC
    • Foodgrain negative growth: 2004-05; also 2009-10, 2012-13, 2014-15, 2015-16.UPPSC
    • Agriculture & allied growth negative: 2014-15 (−0.2%); also 2002-03.UPPSC
    • Agriculture growth 1997-98: about −1%.UPPSC
    • Third Five Year Plan: agriculture growth −1.0%.UPPSC
    • Agriculture growth: 2019-20 6.2%, 2020-21 4.0%, 2022-23 4.7%, 2023-24 0.7%.
    • Foodgrains: 50.8 mn t (1950-51) → 211.9 mn t (2001-02); near self-sufficiency, little bulk import.UPPSC ×2
    • Foodgrains: record 329.69 mn t (2022-23); 309.35 mn t (2023-24, 2nd A.E.).
    • National but not household food security: enough stock, but poor households lack access.UPPSC
    • Reforms needed to feed population; many farmers still rely on monsoon and soil fertility (true, not reason).UPPSC
    • CAG report 2000: food subsidy Rs. 2,800 cr (1992-93) → Rs. 8,700 cr (1998-99), 3.1 times.UPPSC ×3
    • Food subsidy: Rs. 2,05,250 cr (2024-25 Interim BE).

    Horticulture and Plantation

    • China = largest vegetable and fruit producer; India second.UPPSC
    • India first in ginger, okra, banana, mango, papaya; second in potato, onion, cauliflower, brinjal, cabbage.
    • Onion export 2015-16: ~12 lakh tonnes (APEDA).UPPSC

    Agricultural Trade

    • Agri exports 3 categories: traditional, non-traditional with uncertainty, non-traditional with good prospects.UPPSC
    • Traditional: cashew, coffee, tea, fruits, spices, castor oil, raw cotton, sugar, tobacco.
    • Good prospects: meat, flowers, processed fruit/vegetables, wheat, rice, HPS groundnut, oil meals, sesame, niger.
    • Largest agri import by value: vegetable/edible oils (>50% of agri imports).
    • Edible oil imports exceed domestic production; customs duty being cut to lower prices.
    • Edible oil import 2022-23: 164.7 lakh t (SEA); India ~10% of world oilseeds.
    • Lentil (masoor) = largest pulse import in 2015-16, 2019-20, 2020-21.UPPSC
    • India = largest producer and consumer of pulses.
    • Basmati rice = largest forex earning agri product.UPPSC

    Role in Economy

    • Productivity raised by efficient irrigation, quality seeds, pesticides, fertilisers.
    • Low productivity causes: population pressure, small holdings, disguised unemployment, monsoon dependence; not co-operative farming.UPPSC ×2
    • Agriculture matters for national income, employment, industry, trade, food supply.UPPSC
    • Agri share in exports 11.9% (2021-22); employs ~55% workforce (Census 2011; 58.2% in 2001).
    • 2023-24 (2nd A.E.): per capita GDP Rs. 2,10,679 current; wheat 112.02, rice 123.82 mn t.
    • Agricultural income tax: only State Governments (List II, item 46); exempt under IT Act Sec 10(1).UPPSC
    • UP: 59.3% workers in agriculture (Census 2011).UPPSC
    • Cash crop: grown for sale; jute, groundnut, sugarcane; jowar = coarse foodgrain, not cash crop.

    Farm Schemes

    • Vishesh Krishi and Gram Udyog Yojana (VKGUY): promotes agri exports; offsets transport cost.UPPSC
    • Vishesh Krishi Upaj Yojana: boost to export of agricultural produce.UPPSC ×2
    • Kisan Bahi Yojana in UP: 1992.UPPSC
    • RKVY: launched August 2007; Rs. 25,000 cr outlay in 11th Plan.
    • RKVY till 2013-14: 100% central assistance (Centre 100%, State 0%), not 80% grant.UPPSC ×2
    • RKVY from 2015-16: Centre:State 60:40 (NE/Himalayan 90:10; UTs 100%); RKVY-RAFTAAR from 2017-18.
    • RKVY covers soil test labs, fertiliser quality labs, tool test labs, agri engineering.
    • Sengupta and Sdasyuk (1968): 4 macro, 11 meso, 60 micro agricultural regions.UPPSC
    • Planning Commission 1988: 15 agro-climatic zones (8th Plan).
    • National Horticulture Mission: May 2005, 10th Plan; centrally sponsored.UPPSC ×2
    • NHM in 18 States + 5 UTs incl. UP; NE and Himalayan States under separate HMNEH.UPPSC
    • NHM aims: horticulture growth, post-harvest management, human resources; not financial assistance.UPPSC
    • NHM now a sub-scheme of MIDH (2014-15, 12th Plan).
    • Krishi Shramik Samajik Suraksha Yojana (1 July 2001): pension and insurance for farm workers.UPPSC
    • Small Farmer Development Agency (SFDA): 1971, for small/marginal farmers and labourers.
    • NFSA 2013: covers up to 75% rural, 50% urban (~2/3 population); focus on women and children nutrition.UPPSC
    • NFSA: eldest woman aged 18+ = household head for ration card.
    • NFSA: 5 kg/person/month at Rs. 3/2/1 for rice/wheat/coarse grains; AAY 35 kg/household.
    • NFSA: pregnant/lactating women get take-home ration 600 kcal + Rs. 6,000 maternity benefit.
    • NFSA beneficiaries chosen by SECC method, not BPL only; 4 schedules.
    • NFSA Sec 16: State Food Commission in each State (chair + 5 members + member-secretary).
    • Delhi first to launch e-ration card service (March 2015).UPPSC
    • Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 replaced Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954.
    • FSSAI: under Health Ministry; independent chairperson of Secretary rank.
    • NFSM: launched October 2007; aims more rice, wheat, pulses, coarse cereals; soil fertility; farm profits.
    • NFSM tools: HYV seeds, technology demos, new varieties; not credit facilities.UPPSC
    • NFSM effective from Rabi 2007-08; 11th Plan target +20 mn t (rice 10, wheat 8, pulses 2).UPPSC
    • NFSM: coarse cereals added 2014-15; commercial crops (cotton, jute, sugarcane) in 12th Plan.
    • NFSM 8 components (from 2018-19): rice, wheat, pulses, coarse cereals, nutri-cereals, commercial crops, oilseeds & oilpalm, seed village.
    • Raising PDS issue price reduces the subsidy burden.UPPSC

    MSP and Prices

    • FRP (Fair and Remunerative Price) for sugarcane replaced SMP from 2009-10 (Sugarcane Control Order 1966 amended 22.10.2009).
    • FRP approved by CCEA on CACP advice.UPPSC
    • Sugar and sugarcane = essential commodities (Essential Commodities Act 1955).
    • FCI economic cost = acquisition cost (MSP + bonus + procurement incidentals) + distribution cost.
    • MSP for 22 crops by CACP: 7 cereals, 5 pulses, 7 oilseeds, 3 commercial (copra, cotton, jute) + FRP sugarcane.
    • Cereals: paddy, wheat, maize, jowar, bajra, barley, ragi; pulses: gram, tur, moong, urad, lentil.
    • Oilseeds: groundnut, rapeseed-mustard, soyabean, sesamum, sunflower, safflower, nigerseed.
    • Toria and de-husked coconut MSP set by Food Dept from mustard and copra (24 in all).
    • MSP procurement mostly rice, wheat, some pulses, in few States; MSP uniform nationwide.
    • Niger (ramtil): Kharif oilseed with MSP; tribals use its oil.
    • Since 1997-98, MSP > C2 cost (all costs incl. family labour, own land rent, capital interest).
    • CACP: set up January 1965 as Agricultural Prices Commission; renamed CACP 1985.UPPSC
    • MSP recommended by CACP; govt fixes it yearly.UPPSC ×2

    Agricultural Credit

    • Interest Subvention (2006-07): crop loan up to Rs. 3 lakh at 7%; Budget 2011-12 prompt-repayment relief 3% → effective 4%.UPPSC
    • Modified 2022: lenders get 1.5% subvention (2022-23 to 2024-25); farmers still pay 4%.
    • Farm running cost: seed, fertiliser, irrigation water; not land revenue.UPPSC
    • Rural economy helped by pastoralism, cottage industry, good tools; private money-lending adds little.UPPSC
    • Principles of agricultural finance: purpose, person, productivity planning.UPPSC
    • Institutional sources: co-operatives, commercial banks, RRBs, govt; non-institutional: moneylenders, relatives, traders.

    Chapter 6

    Tertiary Sector

    What the services sector covers and its rising share in India's GDP and jobs.

    UPPSC asks most here

    1. Largest GDP share: services; order Services > Industry > Agriculture.PCS Pre ’05, ’12; PCS Mains ’04, ’174 papers
    2. Tertiary includes trade, transport, finance, real estate; not forestry or fishing.PCS Pre ’03; PCS Mains ’04; UDA/LDA ’023 papers
    3. Primary: agriculture, forestry, fishing, dairy, mining; India's primary sector = agriculture.PCS Pre (Re-exam) ’151 paper
    4. Service sector includes transport, communication, hotels; not mining or forestry.PCS Mains ’041 paper
    5. Marketing = tertiary activity; forestry and farming primary; manufacturing secondary.Lower Sub ’081 paper

    Sectors of the economy

    • Primary: agriculture, forestry, fishing, dairy, mining; India's primary sector = agriculture.UPPSC
    • Secondary: manufacturing; turns raw materials into finished goods.
    • Tertiary (services): trade, hotels, transport, communication, banking, insurance, real estate, public administration, defence, education, tourism.
    • Tertiary includes trade, transport, finance, real estate; not forestry or fishing.UPPSC ×3
    • Service sector includes transport, communication, hotels; not mining or forestry.UPPSC
    • Marketing = tertiary activity; forestry and farming primary; manufacturing secondary.UPPSC
    • Transport, communication, commerce = tertiary activities.UPPSC

    Share of services in GDP

    • Services = largest source of national income: 54.9% of nominal GVA (Rs 146.35 of 266.78 lakh crore), 2023-24 (2nd AE).UPPSC

    Chapter 7

    Fiscal Policy and Revenue

    Budget, deficits, GST and other taxes, FRBM Act and Finance Commissions.

    UPPSC asks most here

    1. Interest payments = largest item of revenue and total spending (2015-16 Non-Plan; still 2024-25).PCS Pre ’99, ’05; PCS Mains ’06, ’10, ’15, ’17; PCS Mains (Spl) ’08; Lower Sub (Spl) ’048 papers
    2. Largest tax source in 2005-06, 2007-08, 2009-10, 2013-14: Corporation Tax.PCS Mains ’05, ’06, ’09; PCS Mains (Spl) ’08; Lower Sub ’155 papers
    3. Central Plan outlay 2010-11 order: Energy > Social Services > Transport > Rural Development.PCS Pre ’01, ’02; PCS Mains ’09; UDA/LDA ’024 papers
    4. Economic Survey: by Ministry of Finance (DEA), under Chief Economic Adviser; tabled before Budget.PCS Mains ’10, ’15; UDA/LDA (Spl) ’103 papers
    5. Fiscal deficit = largest deficit; always higher than revenue deficit.PCS Pre ’02; PCS Mains ’04, ’083 papers

    Budget themes and fiscal deficit trend

    • Macro-Economic Framework Statement: placed with Budget; mandated by FRBM Act 2003, section 3(5).
    • Gender budgeting: started Union Budget 2005-06 (4.8% of outlay); 6.5% in 2024-25 (Rs 3.10 lakh crore).
    • Budget 2017-18 ten themes: farmers, rural population, youth, poor, infrastructure, financial sector, digital economy, public services, fiscal management, tax administration; not export performance.UPPSC
    • Budget 2017-18 agenda: TEC India = Transform, Energise, Clean India (not Educate).
    • Budget 2023-24 seven priorities (Saptarishi): inclusive development, last mile, infrastructure, unleashing potential, green growth, youth power, financial sector.
    • AIDC (Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess), Budget 2021-22: on 29 products (gold, silver, petrol, diesel, imported pulses etc.).UPPSC
    • Economic Survey 2015-16 Chakravyuha challenge: "socialism with limited entry to marketism without exit".UPPSC
    • Budget 2023-24: States allowed fiscal deficit 3.5% of GSDP (0.5% tied to power reforms).UPPSC
    • FD 2017-18 above Budget target, as GST start slowed indirect tax growth.UPPSC

    Goods and Services Tax

    • GST first proposed by Vijay Kelkar task force (FRBM, 2004).
    • GST benefit: replaces many taxes → single national market; not big CAD cut.
    • GST = single, multi-stage, destination-based indirect tax on supply; from 1 July 2017.UPPSC
    • GST subsumed Service Tax, Central Excise, State VAT.
    • GST by 101st Constitution Amendment Act, 2016 (122nd Amendment Bill).UPPSC
    • GST was earlier proposed from 1 April 2012 (as of 2009).
    • GST gains: uniform market, better tax compliance, wider tax base, no cascading, ease of business.UPPSC
    • GST Council (Article 279A): chaired by Union FM; MoS Revenue/Finance and State finance ministers members.UPPSC
    • GST Council decides rates, exemptions, threshold; States cannot levy VAT after GST.
    • Outside GST: customs duty, alcohol for drinking, petroleum products, electricity; ghee is inside.
    • GST collection Oct 2020: Rs 1,05,155 crore (over Rs 1 lakh crore); record April 2024: Rs 2,10,267 crore.UPPSC
    • Revenue Neutral Rate: GST rate giving same revenue as old taxes.UPPSC
    • ITC (Input Tax Credit): credit of tax paid on inputs by registered person; avoids cascading.UPPSC
    • ITC allowed for taxable and zero-rated (exports, SEZ) supplies; not for non-taxable, exempt, nil-rated.
    • Project Saksham (CCEA, Sept 2016): new indirect tax IT network of CBEC; Rs 2,256 crore.UPPSC

    Fiscal policy basics

    • Fiscal policy formulated by Ministry of Finance; monetary policy by RBI.UPPSC
    • Long-term fiscal policy: FM V.P. Singh, Budget 1985-86.UPPSC
    • Finance Ministry 6 departments: Economic Affairs, Expenditure, Revenue, DIPAM, Financial Services, Public Enterprises (no Banking Division).
    • Fiscal policy aims: growth, full employment, fair distribution, price stability; not inter-state trade regulation.UPPSC
    • Fiscal policy = taxation, public expenditure, public debt, deficit financing; interest rate = monetary tool.
    • Keynes (General Theory, 1936): fiscal policy to fight Great Depression.
    • Fiscal stimulus: strong govt action to boost economic activity.
    • In recession: raise spending on public projects, cut taxes (ES 2020-21).

    Budget documents and making

    • Budget prepared and presented by Department of Economic Affairs (Finance Ministry).
    • Economic Survey: by Ministry of Finance (DEA), under Chief Economic Adviser; tabled before Budget.UPPSC ×3

    • Zero-based budgeting (ZBB): justify every expense afresh; Peter Pyhrr, 1970s.UPPSC
    • ZBB first in USA: Jimmy Carter (Georgia, 1973); US federal 1976.
    • India ZBB: Dept of Science and Technology 1983; govt-wide 1986; reviews every scheme.UPPSC

    Receipts and expenditure

    • Capital receipts < revenue receipts (2010-11; 2024-25: revenue 63%, capital 37%).UPPSC
    • Public revenue: taxes, VAT, borrowing; subsidy = expenditure, not revenue.UPPSC
    • Revenue (current) receipts: corporation tax, excise, customs, GST, PSU profits, dividends, interest.UPPSC
    • Capital receipts: create liability or cut assets: market loans, NSC sale, World Bank/foreign loans, small savings, disinvestment, loan recovery.
    • Capital spending: assets (roads, machines), loans to States and UTs.
    • Old Non-Plan spending: interest, subsidies, defence, salaries, pensions, maintenance, transfers to States.
    • Budget 2017-18 reforms: Budget on 1 Feb; Railway Budget merged; Plan/Non-Plan split ended.UPPSC
    • 2017-18 did not increase centrally sponsored schemes.
    • Largest Budget item: revenue expenditure.UPPSC
    • Cut deficit: reduce revenue spending, rationalise subsidies, downsize bureaucracy, sell PSU shares.
    • Raise deficit: new welfare schemes, lower import duty.
    • Revenue expenditure: creates no assets (salaries, pensions, subsidies, interest).
    • Interest payments = largest item of revenue and total spending (2015-16 Non-Plan; still 2024-25).UPPSC ×8

    • FD 2017-18 raised 3.2 → 3.5%; 2018-19 target 3.3%; 2020-21 projected 3.0% (not 3.1%).UPPSC

    • States' combined fiscal deficit: 4.1% GDP (2020-21); 2.8% (2021-22, 2022-23); 3.1% (2023-24 BE, Rs 9.48 lakh crore).

    • UP Budget 2024-25: Rs 7,36,437.71 crore; fiscal deficit Rs 86,530.51 crore.
    • High govt borrowing → high real interest rates, less private investment.

    Types of deficit

    • Order of size: Fiscal > Revenue > Primary deficit.UPPSC ×2
    • Fiscal deficit = largest deficit; always higher than revenue deficit.UPPSC ×3
    Deficit (% GDP)2022-232023-24 RE2024-25 BE
    Fiscal6.45.85.1
    Revenue3.92.82.0
    Primary3.02.31.5
    • Budget deficit = total expenditure − total receipts; dropped from 1997-98 Budget.
    • Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts; borrowing for spending that creates no assets.
    • Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts) = total borrowing need.
    • Non-debt capital receipts: loan recoveries, disinvestment receipts.
    • Fiscal deficit = budget deficit + internal and external borrowings; so greater than budget deficit.
    • GFD (financing side) = net home borrowing + RBI borrowing + foreign borrowing.
    • Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments.UPPSC ×2
    • Fiscal deficit = primary deficit + interest payments.UPPSC
    • Primary deficit zero → borrowing = interest payments only.
    • Primary deficit 2010-11: below 2.0% of GDP; 2024-25 target 1.5%.UPPSC
    • Effective Revenue Deficit = revenue deficit − grants for capital assets; from Budget 2011-12.UPPSC
    • ERD added to FRBM Act by 2012 amendment; 0.8% GDP (2024-25 BE).
    • Fiscal deficit mostly filled by domestic borrowing (98–99%); market borrowing (G-Secs) largest.UPPSC
    • Deficit financing → more money supply than goods → inflation.UPPSC ×3
    • Most inflationary: creating new money to fund deficit; public borrowing is less so.
    • In India deficit financing aims at economic development.
    • Subsidy is big source of deficit, but Indian farm subsidy is lower than in Western countries.UPPSC
    • India has long history of fiscal deficits; farm subsidies not larger than West's.UPPSC

    Budget in Parliament

    • Money Bill (Article 110): taxes, borrowing, custody of Consolidated and Contingency Funds; appropriation only from Consolidated Fund.
    • Cut Motion = Budget-related motion in Lok Sabha against a demand for grants.UPPSC ×2
    Cut motionDemand reduced
    Policy cutto Re 1
    Economy cutby a specified amount
    Token cutby Rs 100
    • Vote on Account: advance grant for short-term spending until Budget passes; not sanction of all demands.UPPSC
    • Outcome Budget (from 2005): monitored jointly by Finance Ministry and Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog).UPPSC
    • Performance Budget: from USA (Hoover Commission, 1949).UPPSC
    • Ad hoc Treasury Bills ended 31 March 1997; replaced by Ways and Means Advances (WMA) from 1 April 1997.
    • Public Accounts Committee: audit of Budget via CAG reports; 22 members (15 LS, 7 RS).
    • FRBM Review Committee (N.K. Singh, 2017): general govt debt 60% of GDP by 2023 (Centre 40, States 20).
    • FRBM Act: enacted Aug 2003; in force 5 July 2004; cut fiscal and revenue deficits, debt.UPPSC
    • FRBM: 3-year rolling targets; FD 3% goal; aim below 4.5% by 2025-26.
    • FRBM target: tax-GDP 12% by 2008-09.UPPSC
    • FRBM had: end revenue deficit by 2007-08; no RBI borrowing; cap on guarantees; not end primary deficit.

    Disinvestment and railway budget

    • Disinvestment target 2020-21: Rs 2.1 lakh crore; PSBs and financial institutions Rs 90,000 crore.UPPSC
    • 2000-01: target Rs 10,000 crore; realised only Rs 1,829 crore.UPPSC
    • Railway Budget 2016-17: SRESTHA research body for guided transport.UPPSC
    • Railway Budget 2013-14: Anubhuti hyper-luxury coaches in Rajdhani, Shatabdi.UPPSC

    Taxes: basics and ratios

    • Direct Tax Code: to replace Income Tax Act 1961 and Wealth Tax Act; Akhilesh Ranjan task force 2019.UPPSC
    • Expenditure tax first suggested by Kaldor (also wealth, gift taxes); abolished April 1962.UPPSC
    • Capital gains: rise in asset value (property, painting); sale of inherited property taxed; no inheritance tax.
    • Direct taxes ~5% of GNP (2004); 2024-25 BE: direct 6.7%, indirect 4.9% of GDP.UPPSC
    • Combined tax-GDP ~15% (2004); Centre gross tax-GDP 11.5% (2021-22).
    • Tax-GDP 2008-09: 16.39% (Centre + States, ~16.5%).UPPSC
    • Income redistribution: progressive taxation + progressive expenditure.
    • Indian tax system: progressive but overall degressive; income tax slabs nil, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30%.
    • Indirect taxes = regressive: same rate for all income groups.UPPSC
    • Income tax: direct, progressive; levied and collected by Union (not States); not proportional.UPPSC ×2

    VAT and service tax

    • VAT: tax on value added at each stage from production to final sale; multi-point, destination-based.UPPSC ×2
    • VAT borne by final consumer; a State subject (not Central); ended cascading.
    • VAT from 1 April 2005 (L.K. Jha Indirect Taxation Enquiry Committee 1978).UPPSC
    • Haryana first VAT State (April 2003); UP last (2008).
    • 7 States stayed out initially: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Tamil Nadu, UP.UPPSC
    • Among AP, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, UP: Chhattisgarh, UP had no VAT in 2005.UPPSC
    • Wealth tax: Wealth Tax Act 1957; abolished 2015-16 → surcharge on super-rich.
    • Service tax: indirect; from 1 July 1994 (1994-95), on Raja J. Chelliah Committee advice.UPPSC
    • Service tax rate: 10 → 12% (Budget 2006-07); 14% (2015-16) + 0.5% Swachh + 0.5% Krishi Kalyan cess.UPPSC
    • Services taxed: 110 in 2009-10; 117 (2010-11), 119 (2011-12); negative list from 2012-13.UPPSC ×2

    Direct and indirect taxes

    • Income Tax first introduced 1860 by James Wilson; 4 schedules of income.UPPSC
    • Direct tax: impact and incidence on same person; cannot be shifted: income, corporation, wealth, gift, property, capital gains.UPPSC ×2
    • Indirect tax: can be shifted to buyer: customs, excise, service tax, sales tax, GST, VAT, octroi.UPPSC
    • Income tax does not directly raise prices to buyers; excise, import duty, trade tax do.UPPSC
    • Tax on imports and exports = customs duty.UPPSC ×2
    • Fringe Benefit Tax (2005–2009), Interest Tax (1974 Act), STT (Securities Transaction Tax, 1 Oct 2004): direct taxes.
    • Old sales tax: imposed and collected by State. GST: intra-state CGST + SGST; inter-state IGST (Centre).
    • Corporate income taxes: FBT, MAT, company profit tax; capital gains tax is investor's, not corporate.UPPSC
    • Entertainment tax: State List; not Union.UPPSC
    • Corporation tax: Union only; not levied by States.UPPSC
    • State taxes: land revenue, registration fee, commercial tax, entertainment, agricultural income tax; not customs.
    • Excise duty on liquor: imposed by State Governments (State List).UPPSC
    • Commodity Transaction Tax (CTT): Budget 2013-14; 0.01% on non-farm commodity futures.
    • AGR (Adjusted Gross Revenue) of telecom: all revenue incl. interest, dividend, forex gain (SC, Oct 2019).UPPSC
    • Gratuity Act 1972: firms with 10+ workers; max Rs 10 lakh then; Rs 25 lakh from 1 Jan 2024.
    • Income Declaration Scheme 2016: ~Rs 65,250 crore black money declared by 30 Sept 2016.UPPSC

    Chapter 8

    Planning

    Planning bodies (Planning Commission, NDC, NITI Aayog), early plans, and targets of each Five Year Plan.

    UPPSC asks most here

    1. NDC (National Development Council): set up 6 August 1952, parallel to Planning Commission (not its organ).PCS Pre (Spl) ’08; PCS Mains ’16; RO/ARO Mains ’21; RI ’144 papers
    2. NDC: apex body to approve Five Year Plans; final approving authority.PCS Pre ’01, ’03; PCS Mains ’04, ’084 papers
    3. 11th Plan: 2007-12; theme "Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth".PCS Mains ’08, ’11, ’15; Lower Sub ’084 papers
    4. 11th Plan outlay Rs 36,44,718 cr; highest allocation social services, then energy.PCS Pre ’10; PCS Mains (Spl) ’08; PCS Mains ’083 papers
    5. Tenth (2002-07) · 8.0 · 7.6PCS Mains ’07, ’09; PCS Mains (Spl) ’083 papers

    Planning bodies and their status

    • Economic and Social Planning: in Concurrent List (List-III), Seventh Schedule.UPPSC ×2
    • Planning Commission: set up March 1950 (15 March) by Cabinet Resolution.UPPSC ×2
    • Planning Commission: advisory, non-constitutional, non-statutory (no Act of Parliament) body.
    • Planning Commission described as quasi-political body (not fully independent of govt).UPPSC
    • Ashok Chandra called Planning Commission the "Economic Cabinet of India".UPPSC
    • PM = ex-officio Chairman of Planning Commission; nominated Deputy Chairman with Cabinet Minister rank.
    • No mention in Constitution; no fixed tenure or qualification for Deputy Chairman and members.
    • Deputy Chairmen: Manmohan Singh (1985–87), Pranab Mukherjee (1991–96), Montek S. Ahluwalia (2004–14); P. Chidambaram never.
    • Finance Commission = constitutional, revenue side only (Art. 275 grants); Planning Commission saw capital and revenue.
    • Planning Commission dissolved 1 January 2015.
    • Committee on India Vision 2020 (June 2000): chaired by S.P. Gupta, Planning Commission member.
    • Planning bodies: NDC and Parliament; Plan approved by NDC, then placed in Parliament.
    • NDC (National Development Council): set up 6 August 1952, parallel to Planning Commission (not its organ).UPPSC ×4
    • NDC: apex body to approve Five Year Plans; final approving authority.UPPSC ×4
    • NDC also reviewed Plan working; PM = ex-officio Chairman.

    NITI Aayog

    • NITI = National Institution for Transforming India; set up 1 Jan 2015 by Cabinet Resolution, replaced Planning Commission.
    • NITI: public policy think tank; based on cooperative federalism, bottom-up approach.
    • NITI has no full-time Chairman; PM = ex-officio Chairperson; full-time Vice Chairman.UPPSC
    • Governing Council: PM, CMs of all States and UTs with legislature, LGs of other UTs, VC, members, special invitees.
    • NITI Aayog = nodal institution for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in India.UPPSC
    • First Vice-Chairman: Arvind Panagariya (Jan 2015–Aug 2017); Suman Bery since 1 May 2022.UPPSC ×2
    • CEOs: Sindhushree Khullar (first), Amitabh Kant (from 17 Feb 2016), B.V.R. Subrahmanyam (from 25 Feb 2023).
    • DMEO (Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office): 18 Sept 2015, attached office of NITI Aayog.UPPSC
    • DMEO = merger of PEO and IEO.
    • NITI replaced Five Year Plans with 3-year action plan, 7-year strategy, 15-year vision.

    Ideas and early plans

    • Planning needed for: balanced socio-economic growth, even spread of benefits, removing regional gaps, best use of resources.UPPSC ×2
    • Imperative planning: command system replaces market; indicative planning: State guides and supports market.
    • Max resources for plan spending came from borrowings.
    • M. Visvesvaraya: first to advocate planning; book "Planned Economy for India" (10-year plan to double income).
    • National Planning Committee (Oct 1938): set up by Subhash Chandra Bose (Haripura); Chairman Nehru.
    • Bombay Plan and Gandhian Plan 1944; People's Plan 1945 (Indian Trade Union); Sarvodaya Plan 1950.
    • Gandhian Plan (1944): Shriman Narayan Agarwal; small units, villages, cottage industries.UPPSC
    • Mahatma Gandhi opposed planned development; wanted local self-sufficiency, simple living.UPPSC
    • Sarvodaya Plan (1950): Jayaprakash Narayan.
    • B.S. Minhas wrote "Planning and the Poor".
    • Yojana monthly: Publications Division, Ministry of I&B; started 1957, editor Khushwant Singh.UPPSC
    • Core sector = selected basic industries: electricity, steel, refinery products, crude oil, coal, cement, natural gas, fertilizers.
    • Plan goals: growth, modernization, self-reliance, less dependence on foreign aid.
    • Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula (8th Plan): population 60%, per capita income 25%, fiscal management 7.5%, special problems 7.5%.UPPSC

    Rolling Plan and plan gaps

    • Rolling Plan: suggested by Gunnar Myrdal for backward countries ("Indian Economic Planning in its Broader Setting").UPPSC
    • Rolling Plan has three parts: current-year plan with budget, 3/4/5-year plan revised yearly, 10/15/20-year perspective plan.UPPSC
    • Rolling Plan: Janata Govt, 1978-79, after ending 5th Plan; flexible.UPPSC
    • Rolling Plan ended 1979 when Janata Govt fell; new 6th Plan 1980-85 by Congress.
    • Plan Holiday: 1966-69, three Annual Plans.
    • Years without a Five Year Plan = 7: 1966-69, 1978-79, 1979-80, 1990-92.UPPSC
    • 12th Plan (2012-17) = last Five Year Plan.

    • 2nd Plan (Mahalanobis Plan): 2- and 4-sector model; Mahalanobis = architect of Indian planning.

    • Industrial Policy 1956: goal of socialistic pattern of society (2nd Plan).
    • 4th Plan: first aimed at self-sustaining growth; aimed to cut concentration of wealth.

    Check Garibi Hatao was Indira Gandhi's 1971 election slogan, during 4th Plan; UPPSC still keys 5th Plan.

    • Order: Green Revolution (1966-67) → Bank nationalization of 14 banks (1969) → Garibi Hatao (5th Plan).UPPSC

    • Twenty Point Programme: 1975; revised 1982, 1986; restructured 2006.UPPSC ×2

    Chapter 9

    Money and Banking

    Covers money supply, inflation, price indices, banks, RBI and monetary policy, capital markets and rural credit.

    UPPSC asks most here

    1. SEBI = regulator of share market and stock exchanges; given powers to stop capital market scams.PCS Pre ’96; PCS Mains (Spl) ’04; PCS Mains ’05, ’124 papers
    2. Gilt-edged market = market of Government securities.PCS Pre ’02, ’08; PCS Mains ’04; Lower Sub ’024 papers
    3. NABARD = apex body for agriculture credit; biggest in farm finance and refinance.PCS Pre ’05; PCS Mains ’14; RO/ARO Mains ’14; Lower Sub (Spl) ’044 papers
    4. 14 banks nationalized (19 July; assets above Rs 50 cr) · 1969PCS Pre ’96, ’07; PCS Mains ’14; UDA/LDA ’064 papers
    5. Decimal coinage: 1 April 1957 ("Naya paisa"); "Naya" dropped 1 June 1964.PCS Pre ’95; PCS Mains ’05, ’103 papers

    New finance terms and digital money

    • InvITs (Infrastructure Investment Trusts): SEBI-regulated pooled infrastructure funds; income taxable; borrowers under SARFAESI Act 2002.
    • Interest Coverage Ratio: firm's ease of paying interest; higher = better; shows present and emerging risk.
    • Insolvency = state of being unable to pay debts; bankruptcy = legal process to sell or reorganize assets.
    • IBBI: regulator of insolvency; set up 1 Oct 2016; powers from Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.
    • Inter-Creditor Agreement (2018, Sunil Mehta Committee): fast resolution of stressed loans of Rs 50 cr+.
    • S4A (2016): RBI scheme to restructure debt of big stressed firms.
    • RBI payment data rule (April 2018): all payment data stored only in India.
    • Neeraj Kumar Gupta Committee (2016): boost cashless transactions.
    • MDR (Merchant Discount Rate): fee bank charges merchant for accepting card payments.
    • NFS (National Financial Switch): links all ATMs; run by NPCI since 2009.
    • NPCI: set up with RBI help for financial inclusion; launched RuPay (2012) and UPI.
    • UPI: instant mobile inter-bank payment; makes mobile wallets unnecessary.
    • CBDC (Central Bank Digital Currency): can bypass US dollar and SWIFT; can carry spending conditions.
    • Bitcoin (Jan 2009, Satoshi Nakamoto): peer-to-peer; not tracked by central banks; parties can stay anonymous.
    • NFTs: unique blockchain tokens; not exchangeable at par, so not a medium of payment.

    Money supply and currency

    • M3 (Broad Money) = currency with public + demand deposits + other deposits with RBI + time deposits = M1 + time deposits.UPPSC
    • RBI publishes M0, M1, M2, M3; M3 = aggregate money supply, most used.
    • Cash withdrawal from bank: money supply unchanged (deposit falls, currency rises).
    • Liquidity order: currency > demand deposits > savings deposits > time deposits.
    • Money multiplier = Broad Money (M3) / Reserve Money (M0).UPPSC ×2
    • Money multiplier rises with banking habit; falls with higher CRR and SLR.
    • Black money: illegal income or unrecorded income on which tax not paid.UPPSC ×2
    • Black money's main worry: revenue loss from tax evasion.
    • Demonetization 8 Nov 2016: old Rs 500 and Rs 1000 notes withdrawn.
    • Demonetization aims: curb black money, fake notes, terror funds; widen tax base; less cash; more digital. Raising GDP growth not an aim.UPPSC
    • Paper Currency Act 1861 gave Govt monopoly of notes; first Govt paper currency 1862.UPPSC
    • Decimal coinage: 1 April 1957 ("Naya paisa"); "Naya" dropped 1 June 1964.UPPSC ×3
    • Legal tender: money a creditor must accept to settle claims.
    • Coins (Coinage Act 2011): Re 1 and above legal tender up to Rs 1000; 50 paise up to Rs 10.
    • RBI can print notes up to Rs 10,000 (Sec 24, RBI Act 1934).UPPSC
    • Rs 10,000 note: 1938 (demonetized 1946) and 1954 (demonetized 1978).
    • Rs 2000 note: Nov 2016; printing stopped 2018-19; withdrawn 2023 but still legal tender.
    • Note issue: Minimum Reserve System (1956) replaced proportional reserve system.UPPSC ×3
    • Since 1957: minimum Rs 200 cr gold and foreign securities, of which gold at least Rs 115 cr.UPPSC
    • Notes backed by gold, rupee coin, GoI securities, foreign securities (Sec 33, RBI Act).
    • Coins issued by Ministry of Finance (GoI); RBI only distributes them.UPPSC
    • Four mints: Mumbai, Noida (UP), Kolkata, Hyderabad.UPPSC

    Inflation basics

    • Currency expansion = more money supply → money loses value → higher prices.
    • Inflation: prices rise, money value falls; exchange rate does not improve.
    • Demand-pull inflation: demand > supply; caused by expansionary policy, fiscal stimulus, higher purchasing power; not by rising interest rates.
    • Fall in inflation rate = prices rising more slowly, not falling.UPPSC
    • Deflation = persistent fall in general price level.
    • Zero inflation for a year only if inflation is zero in every week.
    GroupEffect of inflation
    Debtors, producers, traders, farmers, variable incomesGainUPPSC ×2
    Creditors, consumers, pensioners, fixed incomes, savers, bondholdersLose
    Public spending, imports, taxesRise
    Public savings, exportsFall
    • Inflation fell 10.9% (1994-95) → 4.8% (1997-98); foreign investment rose only slightly.UPPSC
    • Base effect: last year's price level distorts current inflation rate.
    • Double-digit inflation curbed by cutting budget deficit and unproductive spending (early 1990s).
    • Stagflation: high inflation + slow growth + high unemployment.
    • Bottleneck inflation: supply falls sharply, demand same; hard to tackle.UPPSC
    • Cost-push inflation: aggregate supply curve shifts left, e.g. wage rise.
    • Headline inflation: change in CPI basket; core inflation = headline minus food and fuel.UPPSC

    Price indices and inflation control

    • CPI (Combined) = key inflation measure of RBI since April 2014 (Urjit Patel Committee); base 2012 = 100.UPPSC ×3
    • Headline inflation measured on CPI-Combined.UPPSC
    • Earlier WPI was main inflation index; inflation also measured by Labour Cost of Living index.
    • CPI covers goods and services, retail prices; used by RBI/MPC for monetary policy.UPPSC
    • WPI: goods only, no services; food weight WPI 24.4% vs CPI 45.9%.
    • Inflation target: set by GoI with RBI every 5 years (RBI Act amended May 2016).
    • Target 4% CPI ± 2% for 5 Aug 2016–31 March 2021; kept for 2021–2026.

    • CPI-IW base 1982 → 2001 (in 2006) → 2016 (Sept 2020).UPPSC
    • CPI-IW used to fix Dearness Allowance (DA) of Central Govt employees.UPPSC ×3
    • WPI weekly till 2009/2012; now monthly only; gives less weight to food than CPI-IW.
    • WPI base years: 1981-82 → 1993-94 (April 2000) → 2004-05 → 2011-12 (from April 2017).
    • WPI base 2004-05: decided 19 Oct 2009; released 14 Sept 2010; Abhijit Sen Committee.UPPSC ×3
    • WPI 2011-12 weights: manufactured products 64.23% (largest), primary 22.62%, fuel and power 13.15%.UPPSC

    • Producer Price Index (PPI): average change in prices received by producers.UPPSC
    • Raising (not reducing) interest rate controls inflation; cutting rates = expansionary policy.UPPSC
    • Monetary measures: higher interest rate, credit control, money supply control, demonetization.
    • Fiscal measures: cut needless spending, raise taxes, more savings, surplus budget, public debt.
    • Other measures: more production, rational wage policy, price control, rationing, demand control.
    • Less money in circulation helps control inflation.
    • Inflation negative Oct 2009–Feb 2010 as crude fell from $140 to $30 a barrel.UPPSC

    Bank history and nationalization

    • Oudh Commercial Bank (1881, Faizabad): first limited-liability bank fully run by Indians; failed 1958.
    • Punjab National Bank (1894, Lahore; work from 12 April 1895): first Swadeshi bank.

    • Order: SBI → Lead Bank Scheme → RRBs → NABARD.UPPSC

    • Lead Bank Scheme origin: D.R. Gadgil Study Group and F.K.F. Nariman Committee (1969).
    • Rural branches of all banks incl. RRBs: about 37% (30 June 2012); about 36% (March 2023).UPPSC

    Lead Bank and financial inclusion

    • LBS = Lead Bank Scheme: tool of financial inclusion; one bank given lead role per district.UPPSC
    • Lead Bank = bank designated for the district; coordinates credit bodies and Govt.UPPSC
    • LBS aim: each bank adopts certain districts for intensive development; last reviewed by Usha Thorat Committee (2009).
    • District credit planning done under the Lead Bank.UPPSC ×2
    • Service Area Approach (1989): under LBS; each rural branch serves 15–25 villages.
    • SIDBI: 2 April 1990, Act of Parliament; main body for MSME promotion, finance, development.UPPSC ×2
    • SIDBI headquarters: Lucknow.UPPSC ×2
    • Head offices: Allahabad Bank – Kolkata (merged with Indian Bank 2020); Indian Overseas Bank – Chennai; SIDBI – Lucknow (not Mumbai).UPPSC
    • Financial inclusion: basic banking for all incl. zero/minimum-balance accounts and services for low-income groups.UPPSC
    • Inclusion aims: serve poor, unlock weaker sections' growth, reach rural areas, expand (not shrink) bank network.UPPSC
    • Hurdles to inclusion: low income, illiteracy, lack of bank branches.UPPSC
    • Committee on Financial Inclusion: C. Rangarajan (formed 26 June 2006; report 4 Jan 2008).UPPSC ×2
    • Small Finance Banks (RBI guidelines Nov 2014): savings and credit to small business, small and marginal farmers, unorganized sector.
    • Payments Banks: recommended by Nachiket Mor Committee (formed 23 Sept 2013; report 7 Jan 2014).UPPSC
    • Payments Banks: deposits and debit cards; no credit cards, no lending; telcos can promote.
    • Shadow banking: bank-like lending by lightly regulated non-bank intermediaries; term by Paul McCulley 2007.UPPSC
    • NBFI: no full banking licence; mainly term loans for large firms.
    • NBFC: cannot take demand deposits or issue cheques; no DICGC cover.
    • Microfinance: credit, savings, insurance, fund transfer to low-income people.
    • RBI sub-committee on microfinance: Y.H. Malegam (15 Oct 2010).UPPSC
    • Malegam Committee → new category NBFC-MFI (2011).UPPSC
    • Gullak Bachcha Bank: children's bank, Bal Bhavan-Kilkari, Patna (14 Nov 2009).

    Bank balance sheet and loans

    Bank liabilitiesBank assets
    Paid-up capital and reservesCash in hand and with RBI
    Deposits: time and demandMoney at call and short notice
    BorrowingsInvestments
    Other liabilitiesLoans, advances, credit to farmersUPPSC
    • Deposits = liability, not asset.
    • Time deposits = biggest part of bank liabilities.UPPSC ×2
    • NPA (Non-Performing Asset): loan whose interest or principal not recovered; overdue over 90 days.UPPSC
    • Priority sector lending: at least 40% of bank credit; agriculture, MSMEs, weaker sections, education, housing, exports.
    • Loan terms: short up to 1 year (15 months); medium up to 3 (or 5) years; long above that.
    • Teaser loans: low starting-rate home loans; sub-prime default risk.
    • Internal debt: market borrowings, Treasury bills, special securities to RBI.
    • Core Banking Solutions: networked branches; operate account from any branch.
    • GoI bought RBI's 59.7% stake in SBI (June 2007).UPPSC
    • RBI sold NABARD stake (2010, 2019) and NHB stake (19 March 2019); GoI now owns 100% of both.
    • National Housing Bank: 9 July 1988 under NHB Act 1987; was RBI's wholly owned subsidiary.
    • Basel Committee: 1974, G10 central banks; at BIS, Basel.
    • Basel II (2004): international standards for bank capital adequacy; Basel I 1988.UPPSC
    • Basel III: after 2007-09 crisis; helps banks handle stress and manage risk.
    • Basel II three pillars: minimum capital, supervisory review, market discipline through disclosure.
    • CAR / CRAR (Capital Adequacy Ratio): bank capital vs risk-weighted assets; set by regulators, not banks.
    • CRAR: Basel III 8%; RBI 9% (11.5% with capital conservation buffer).
    • DICGC: RBI subsidiary (Act 1961); insures deposits up to Rs 5 lakh per depositor since 4 Feb 2020.UPPSC
    • Savings account interest deregulated Oct 2011; banks now fix it.
    • MCLR (Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate): from 1 April 2016; banks cannot lend below it; transparency, fairness.

    RBI: role and functions

    • RBI: set up 1 April 1935 under RBI Act 1934; HQ Kolkata, moved to Mumbai 1937; nationalized 1949.UPPSC ×2
    • RBI = apex bank; regulates money supply; supervises NABARD; does not lend to business families.UPPSC
    • RBI = bankers' bank: holds banks' deposits, lends in need, advises them.UPPSC
    • RBI = fiscal agent and adviser to Govt; banker to Centre and States; manages public debt.UPPSC
    • RBI = Govt agent for India's IMF membership; runs Govt borrowing programme.
    • RBI banker to all States and UTs Puducherry and J&K except Sikkim (limited agreement only).
    • RBI keeps foreign exchange reserves.UPPSC
    • RBI controls credit creation of commercial banks.UPPSC
    • Credit creation = function of commercial banks, not RBI.UPPSC
    • RBI controls money and credit by quantitative and qualitative tools.UPPSC
    • Foreign trade regulated by Ministry of Commerce, not RBI.
    • Lender of last resort: RBI gives liquidity to solvent banks in temporary crisis.
    • RBI issues all notes except Re 1 note; Re 1 note issued by GoI.UPPSC
    • Re 1 note signed by Finance Secretary; other notes by RBI Governor.UPPSC
    • Treasury bills: short-term (under 1 year) GoI debt; zero coupon, issued at discount; first 1917.
    • T-bills sold by RBI through auction; tenors 91, 182, 364 days.UPPSC
    • States issue only dated bonds = State Development Loans (SDLs); RBI manages them too.
    • RBI Retail Direct (Nov 2021): individuals buy G-Secs; NDS-OM = RBI's G-Sec trading platform.

    Monetary policy and credit control

    • Monetary policy complements fiscal policy; works better in inflation, fiscal policy in deflation.UPPSC
    • Monetary policy aims: price stability, economic stability, exchange rate stability; not equal income distribution.UPPSC
    • RBI made monetary policy till 2016; now MPC (Monetary Policy Committee) sets policy rate; RBI keeps price stability.
    • MPC: 6 members (3 RBI incl. Governor, 3 Govt-nominated for 4 years); RBI Governor chairs.
    Quantitative toolsQualitative (selective) tools
    Bank RateMargin requirements
    Open Market OperationsConsumer credit regulation
    Repo and Reverse RepoDirectives
    Marginal Standing FacilityRationing of creditUPPSC
    CRR and SLR (variable reserve ratios)Moral suasion, publicity, direct action
    • OMO (Open Market Operations) = RBI trading in Govt securities and T-bills; quantitative tool.UPPSC ×3
    • RBI buys securities → more money; sells → less money.
    • Bank Rate and OMO = monetary policy; public debt and revenue = fiscal policy.
    • Sterilization: RBI absorbs fresh inflows via OMO (selling T-bills).
    • Operation Twist: RBI sells short-term, buys long-term securities; lowers long-term rates; US Fed 1961.UPPSC
    • Money supply rises: RBI buys Govt securities; Govt borrows from RBI.
    • Money supply falls: public deposits cash in banks; RBI sells securities.
    • RBI fights inflation: raise Bank Rate, Repo, CRR, SLR; sell (not buy) securities.UPPSC
    • Lower interest rate → more investment and consumption spending.

    Reserve ratios, policy rates, Governors

    • Statutory reserve requirements: let RBI control how much credit banks create.
    • SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio): share of deposits kept by bank itself as cash, gold, securities.UPPSC
    • SLR: Sec 24(2A), Banking Regulation Act 1949; helps Govt sell its securities to banks.
    • SLR cut → more lendable cash → banks may cut lending rates.
    • CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio): share of NDTL kept as cash with RBI; no interest; more active tool.UPPSC
    • CRR rise → less liquidity, less bank lending, less credit creation.UPPSC ×2
    • CRR cut → more liquidity, investment, money supply, credit creation.
    • NDTL = Net Demand and Time Liabilities (deposits) of banks.
    • MSF (Marginal Standing Facility): overnight borrowing by dipping into SLR at penal rate; Bank Rate aligned to MSF (Feb 2012).
    • Expansionary policy: cut SLR, Bank Rate, Repo; raising MSF rate is contractionary.
    • PLR (Prime Lending Rate): set by commercial banks for best borrowers, not RBI.UPPSC
    • Financial sector reforms: lower CRR and SLR, free interest rates, private banks and insurers, NPA reforms.
    • After 1991 reforms SLR and CRR both reduced (Narasimham Committee): SLR 38.5% (1991) → 25% (1997).UPPSC
    • CRR 13% (May 1996) → 9% (Nov 1999).
    • Repo Rate: rate at which RBI lends short-term (overnight) to banks against Govt securities, under LAF.UPPSC ×3
    • Repo Rate = key monetary policy tool, regulated by RBI; controls money supply and inflation.UPPSC ×2
    • "Repurchase Option" (Repo) controls money supply, not rupee selling pressure.UPPSC
    • Reverse Repo Rate: rate at which RBI borrows from banks; absorbs surplus money.UPPSC
    • Repo minus Reverse Repo = 1% (June 2010–June 2011); not so now.UPPSC
    • Bank Rate: rate at which RBI rediscounts bills of exchange; RBI loans to banks, longer term.UPPSC ×3
    • Bank Rate rise = tight money policy; Bank Rate cut = more liquidity.

    Financial institutions, insurance, mutual funds

    • Company limited by shares: members' liability limited to unpaid amount on their shares.
    • LLP (Limited Liability Partnership): min 2 partners, no upper limit; perpetual succession; flexible internal rules.

    Markets, prices and business basics

    • Prices are essential for a market; market leads to consumerism.UPPSC
    • Buyer's market: supply > demand.UPPSC
    • Accounting = language of business; gives all information a businessman needs.UPPSC
    • Condition = essential term, breach lets party reject contract; warranty = side term, breach gives only damages.UPPSC
    • Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities; acid test = liquid assets / current liabilities.
    • C2B model: consumers name price, business accepts or declines.
    • Vegetables, flowers, fruits: very short period market (fixed supply).UPPSC
    • Supply-side economics: producer's view; tax cuts raise investment.
    • Total product constant → marginal product zero.UPPSC

    • Price rise: businessmen profit; consumers cut needs (separate facts).UPPSC ×2

    • Commerce: removes hurdles to exchange; delivers goods to consumers.UPPSC

    Chapter 10

    Human Development

    How development is measured beyond income: PQLI, HDI, GII, happiness and State indices.

    UPPSC asks most here

    1. Gross National Happiness: Bhutan, 4th King Jigme Singye Wangchuck, 1970s.PCS Pre ’01, ’03; PCS Mains ’09; UDA/LDA ’024 papers
    2. Not in HDI: health-nutrition, urbanisation, social inequality.PCS Mains (Spl) ’08; PCS Mains ’09; UDA/LDA ’133 papers
    3. EDI 2009-10 (Feb 2011) top States: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Delhi.PCS Mains ’10, ’112 papers
    4. Three stages of society (theological → metaphysical → positive): Auguste Comte.PCS Pre ’211 paper
    5. HDI and SDG ranks of States move together; SDG targets rest on health and education.PCS Pre ’191 paper

    Measures and thinkers

    • Three stages of society (theological → metaphysical → positive): Auguste Comte.UPPSC
    • HDI and SDG ranks of States move together; SDG targets rest on health and education.UPPSC
    • Order: Per-capita Income (USA 1934, Kuznets) → PQLI (1970s) → HDI (1990).
    • PQLI (Physical Quality of Life Index): Morris D. Morris, mid-1970s.UPPSC
    • PQLI = average of literacy, infant mortality, life expectancy at age one; best pair: IMR + literacy.UPPSC
    • Capability Approach: Amartya Sen.

    Human Development Index

    • HDR published by UNDP, first in 1990.UPPSC
    • UNDP first focused on human side of development.UPPSC
    • HDI designed by Mahbub-ul-Haq (Pakistan).UPPSC
    • HDI: life expectancy, education (mean + expected schooling years), GNI per capita PPP $.UPPSC
    • Not in HDI: health-nutrition, urbanisation, social inequality.UPPSC ×3
    • Before 2010: GDP per capita, adult literacy, enrolment; HDI = geometric mean, 0 to 1.
    • Life expectancy limits: 85 and 20 years (25 before 2010).
    • More children in school and adult literacy raise India's HDI rank.UPPSC

    Chapter 11

    Employment and Welfare Schemes

    Government schemes for health, skills, women, rural jobs, social security, sanitation and education.

    UPPSC asks most here

    1. Bharat Nirman 6 parts: irrigation, drinking water, electricity, roads, housing, telephone; no sanitation, schools, hospitals, industry.PCS Pre ’06, ’15; PCS Mains ’06, ’08, ’11, ’16; PCS Mains (Spl) ’087 papers

    Chapter 12

    Poverty and Unemployment

    How India measures poverty and unemployment, key committees, estimates, indices and types of unemployment.

    UPPSC asks most here

    1. Planning Commission 1999-2000: Odisha highest poverty (47.1%).PCS Pre ’03, ’05, ’14; Lower Sub ’02; UDA/LDA ’025 papers
    2. Poverty level fixed by household consumption expenditure.PCS Pre ’09; RO/ARO Mains ’13; Lower Sub ’133 papers
    3. Lowest poverty 2011-12: A&N 1.00, Lakshadweep 2.77, Goa 5.09, Kerala 7.05, HP 8.06, Sikkim, Punjab 8.26.PCS Mains (Spl) ’04; PCS Mains ’11; GIC ’103 papers
    4. Disguised unemployment: more people on a job than needed; marginal productivity zero.PCS Mains ’04; PCS Mains (Spl) ’08; GIC ’103 papers
    5. Poverty in India defined by calorie intake (minimum food basket).PCS Mains ’08; Lower Sub (Spl) ’082 papers

    Measuring poverty in India

    • Poverty types: objective vs subjective; absolute vs relative; transversal (one year) vs persistent (long term).
    • Absolute poverty: cannot afford basic food, housing, clothes; UN definition 1995.
    • World Bank extreme poverty line: US$ 2.15 a day (2017 PPP), from Sept 2022; earlier US$ 1.90 (2011 PPP).
    • Head Count Ratio (HCR): share of population below poverty line.
    • Poverty line based on consumption data, not income (incomes of self-employed and casual workers hard to measure).UPPSC
    • Poverty level fixed by household consumption expenditure.UPPSC ×3
    • Consumption surveys done by NSSO (now NSO); poverty estimated by Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog).
    • State poverty lines updated with CPI-IW (urban) and CPI-AL (rural); differ by State due to price levels.
    • 61st NSS round (2004-05): both Uniform Recall Period (30 days) and Mixed Recall Period (365 days for 5 non-food items).
    • Alagh Task Force (1977, report 1979): poverty line on nutrition needs only.UPPSC
    • Poverty line calories: urban 2100 kcal per person per day.UPPSC
    • Rural poverty line: 2400 kcal per person per day.UPPSC
    • Poverty in India defined by calorie intake (minimum food basket).UPPSC ×2
    • Alagh line (1973-74 prices): Rs 49.09 rural, Rs 56.64 urban per person per month.
    • Tendulkar Committee: set up 2005, report 2009; new poverty estimation standards.UPPSC
    • Tendulkar: dropped calorie norm; one all-India basket for rural and urban; Mixed Reference Period; adds health, education.
    • Tendulkar line 2011-12: Rs 816/month rural (about Rs 26–27/day), Rs 1000 urban (about Rs 32–33/day); poverty 21.9%.
    • Rangarajan Committee: set up 2012, report June 2014; Rs 32/day rural, Rs 47/day urban.
    • Rangarajan: Rs 972 rural, Rs 1407 urban per month; poverty 29.5% (2011-12); government did not adopt it.

    Inequality and poverty concepts

    • Lorenz curve (Max O. Lorenz, 1905): shows income inequality; more sag below 45° line = more inequality.UPPSC
    • Gini coefficient (Corrado Gini): 0 = full equality, 1 = full inequality; derived from Lorenz curve.
    • Culture of Poverty: Oscar Lewis (American anthropologist).UPPSC
    • Vicious Circle of Poverty: Ragnar Nurkse, 1953; low income → low saving → low investment → low productivity.UPPSC
    • Cyclic poor: move in and out of poverty.

    Poverty committees and agencies

    • Poverty line fixed by Planning Commission; NITI Aayog from 1 Jan 2015.UPPSC
    • Planning Commission was nodal agency for national and State poverty estimates.UPPSC
    • Lakdawala Committee (1993): calorie-based consumption; State-specific lines; CPI-IW/CPI-AL updating; stop scaling to National Accounts.

    Anti-poverty measures

    • Ways to remove poverty: more productive investment, more saving, population control.
    • DRDAs: coordinate anti-poverty schemes and watch their funds.
    • PDS: started 1960s as price support; essential goods at subsidised prices.UPPSC
    • PDS food subsidy given by Centre, not States; PDS also checks hoarding and black marketing.
    • Rural anti-poverty programmes: IRDP (1980), TRYSEM (1979), NREP (1980).UPPSC
    • UNDP poverty types: income poverty and human poverty.UPPSC
    • Human Poverty Index: HDR 1997.UPPSC ×2
    • Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI): OPHI + UNDP; replaced HPI in HDR 2010.UPPSC
    • MPI: 3 dimensions, 10 indicators.UPPSC
    • MPI dimensions: health, education, living standard (each 1/3).UPPSC
    MPI dimensionIndicators (weight)
    Healthnutrition, child mortality (1/6 each)

    Living standardcooking fuel, sanitation, water, electricity, housing, assets (1/18 each)
    • MPI best measure of intensity of poverty; household-level, not PPP or deficit.UPPSC
    • HDR 2013: 53.7% Indians multidimensionally poor.UPPSC
    • HDR 2023/24: 16.4% (230.74 million, 2019-21); India has most poor people.
    • Causes of poverty: low growth, fast population growth, unemployment; rising investment reduces poverty.UPPSC
    • Social poverty indicators: illiteracy, poor health access, no jobs; few transport means is not one.UPPSC
    • Differential Interest Rate Scheme (1972): cheap loans to weaker sections.UPPSC
    • May 2013: women SHG loans up to Rs 3 lakh at 7% (under NRLM).UPPSC
    • Hoover Medal 2008 (given March 2009): A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, for uplifting rural poor.UPPSC
    • SHGs and micro-credit: Muhammad Yunus, Grameen Bank; Nobel Peace Prize 2006.
    • SAARC Ministerial Conference on Poverty Alleviation: Islamabad, April 2002.UPPSC
    • Indian social structure: rural majority, many religions, many castes; poverty is socio-economic, not social.UPPSC

    Employment trends

    • After 1991: rural non-farm growth rose; rural job growth fell (1.45% → −0.28%); rural share of workforce 77.8% → 70.9%.
    • Employment growth in India: about 2% a year.UPPSC
    • Unemployment raises poverty: people near the line fall below it.
    • Kerala: highest educated unemployment.
    • Educated unemployment rises with fast growth when professional education is lacking.UPPSC ×2
    • Urban poverty rooted in rural areas: low rural education → poor jobs for migrants.UPPSC
    • Employed urban males 1999-2000 order: West Bengal, Assam, Nagaland, Meghalaya.UPPSC ×2
    • Organised sector jobs: +1.2% a year (1983-94), −0.03% (1994-2007) = declined.UPPSC

    Types and measures of unemployment

    • Most unemployment in India = structural (skills do not match jobs).
    • Disguised unemployment: more people on a job than needed; marginal productivity zero.UPPSC ×3
    • Disguised unemployment: mainly primary sector, i.e. agriculture.UPPSC ×2
    • Disguised unemployment linked to agriculture and rural areas.UPPSC
    • Usual Status: unemployed for major part of the year (365-day reference); long-term open unemployment.UPPSC
    • NSSO measures: Usual Principal Status (1 year), Current Weekly Status (1 week), Current Daily Status (each day); no monthly status.UPPSC ×2
    • Employment-unemployment data published by NSSO; merged with CSO into NSO in 2019.UPPSC
    • Employment elasticity (1999-2000 to 2009-10): construction 1.13, finance 0.66, manufacturing 0.09, agriculture 0.04, all 0.19.
    • Causes of unemployment: population growth, lack of skills, poor manpower planning; not rising per capita income.UPPSC
    • LFPR (Labour Force Participation Rate): people working or seeking work ÷ working-age population.
    • Female LFPR fell: 31.1% (2013-14) → 23.3% (2017-18); due to more education, higher family income.UPPSC

    Chapter 13

    International Trade

    India's foreign trade: size, partners, items, BoP, trade policies, SEZs, export bodies, tourism and trade pacts.

    UPPSC asks most here

    1. Engineering goods: top export item (US$ 112 bn, 2021-22).PCS Pre ’96; PCS Mains ’06; RO/ARO ’14, ’17; RO/ARO Mains ’175 papers
    2. ECGC (1957, Govt-owned): export credit risk insurance → export financing and insurance.PCS Mains (Spl) ’04; PCS Mains ’05, ’09; UDA/LDA ’014 papers
    3. Dept of Commerce long-term vision (FTP 2015-20): make India major player in world trade by 2020.PCS Mains ’14, ’17; RO/ARO Mains ’143 papers
    4. Asia (with ASEAN) = India's largest trade partner region and import source; ~61–63% of imports (2022-24).PCS Mains ’06, ’09; UDA/LDA ’103 papers
    5. Petroleum (crude and products): top import; 29.4% (2022-23), 26.52% (2023-24).PCS Mains ’04; PCS Mains (Spl) ’04; Lower Sub (Spl) ’043 papers

    Basic concepts

    • Rules of Origin: criteria to fix national source of product; used for duties, anti-dumping, MFN vs preferential treatment, trade statistics, labelling, govt procurement.
    • SCRI (Supply Chain Resilience Initiative): India, Japan, Australia; launched 27 April 2021; spreads import-supply risk over many nations.
    • Foreign Trade Policy: under Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
    • Balance of Trade (BoT) = exports − imports of goods only (visible items).UPPSC
    • Net exports = exports − imports; positive = trade surplus, negative = trade deficit.UPPSC
    • Balance of Payments (BoP): account of a country's exports, imports and other transactions with world, usually one year.UPPSC
    • BoP = complete record of all economic transactions between residents of a country and rest of world.UPPSC
    • BoP includes visible trade, invisible trade and borrowings.UPPSC
    • Current account = BoT + balance of invisibles (services, transfers, net income); capital account = investments, borrowings, assets.
    • Current Account Deficit (CAD): payments exceed receipts from goods, services, transfers, net income; happens when country imports more.UPPSC
    • Invisible export = export of services (tourism, banking, insurance, software).UPPSC ×2
    • Foreigners visiting India (e.g. XIX Commonwealth Games) = export (tourism, invisible).
    • Entrepot trade: goods imported, stored, then re-exported without processing or customs duty.UPPSC
    • Tariff: tax on imports; raises import prices → reduces volume of trade.UPPSC
    • Duty drawback: refund of customs/excise duty on inputs used to make export goods.UPPSC
    • Closed economy: neither exports nor imports.
    • Import quota = physical control; Open General Licence → external trade; CRR → debt control; WPI → inflation; TRYSEM → employment.
    • Super 301 (Special 301): annual US (USTR) list of foreign trade barriers; means blockade in free trade.UPPSC
    • Anti-dumping duty: against exports sold below normal value; WTO permits it.
    • India used maximum anti-dumping measures in 1995-2005; now USA top (493 in 2022), India 2nd (142).UPPSC

    Size and share of trade

    • Dept of Commerce long-term vision (FTP 2015-20): make India major player in world trade by 2020.UPPSC ×3
    • FTP 2023 target: overall exports US$ 2 trillion by 2030.
    • Trade-to-GDP ratio (World Bank): above 50% only in 2008, 2011–2013; lowest 7.66% (1970); 40% (2019), 46% (2023).
    • Merchandise trade/GDP: 29.5% (2004-05) → 40.6% (2012-13); 31.1% in 2023.UPPSC ×2
    • Goods trade/GDP: 14.2% (1990-91) → almost three times by 2011-12.UPPSC
    • Exports of goods and services ≈ 22% of GDP (2010-11); 21.9% in 2023.UPPSC
    • India's share in world exports: 1.85% (1950) → 0.5–0.7% in 1990s.UPPSC
    • Share in world merchandise exports: 1.7% (2018, 2019), 1.6% (2020), 1.8% (2021, 2022); rank 18 exports, 9 imports (2022).
    • Commercial services exports: India 8th (2014, 2019), 7th (2022, 4.4% share).
    • Merchandise exports 2021-22 US$ 422 bn vs imports US$ 613 bn; services exports > services imports.
    • Export growth: ~18% (1994-95).UPPSC
    • Highest export growth among 2002-06: 2004-05 (30.8%).UPPSC
    • Export growth: −1.6% (2001-02), −6.9% (2020-21), +44.6% (2021-22), −3.09% (2023-24).
    • Slow export growth causes: high price, foreign competition, low-quality goods.UPPSC
    • Trade balance negative every year since 1949-50 except 1972-73 and 1976-77.
    • Trade deficit peak US$ 195.66 bn (2012-13), then fell till 2016-17 as POL and non-POL deficits fell.UPPSC
    • Trade deficit: US$ 264.89 bn (2022-23), 240.17 bn (2023-24).

    Globalisation and liberalisation

    • Globalisation: dismantling barriers in international trade.UPPSC
    • Globalisation of Indian economy: minimum restrictions on economic relations with other countries.UPPSC

    • Free Trade Zones: set up to promote export industries.UPPSC ×3
    • FTZ: industries free from excise duty, produce for export.UPPSC
